problem: End-to-end RL image-goal navigation policies match goal and observation images and directly output actions; when the goal is far or in another room there is little visual overlap, so they get no informative cues and wander or backtrack. Modular methods need extra sensors (depth, pose) and suffer error accumulation.
motivation: Humans use slow deliberate reasoning (System 2) to form coarse plans (e.g., exit the room) that constrain fast reactive execution (System 1). Adding such short-horizon planning to a single-RGB agent could extract cues from limited inputs without extra sensors and reduce aimless wandering on long-horizon episodes. Zero-shot VLMs give limited gains, so task-specific finetuning with short-horizon plan data is needed.
key_idea: Decompose image-goal navigation into a finetuned VLM slow planner that outputs short-horizon sub-task instructions every 15 steps, and a lightweight RL fast executor conditioned on that plan and trained with a Wandering Suppression Penalty.
insight: The slow planner helps: removing it drops SPL from 66.21 to 63.53 on Gibson, and swapping in Qwen2 drops it to 55.29, so task-specific finetuning matters. The planner is also far more accurate on the held-out planning set than Qwen2-VL/Qwen3-VL (CIDEr 2.74 vs 0.13/0.23). Gains grow with difficulty (Hard SPL +7.4 on Gibson, +9.0 on MP3D). WSP must be applied after ZER warm-up and with a moderate weight; λ_w=1.0 collapses to 71.83 SR, and revisit + path-length penalties are complementary (SPL 66.21 → 71.15). The planner is queried sparsely, so latency is amortized (24 FPS at k=15).
method: Hierarchical Reasoning Dataset: Qwen3-14B decomposes R2R-CE/RxR-CE instructions into atomic sub-tasks; Qwen2.5-VL-32B temporally grounds them on frames overlaid with timestamp and action; the last frame is the goal image; the label is the sub-task active in a short future window. The result is 198K RxR + 239K xsR2R + 330K YouTube samples before filtering.
Triple Quality Control (TQCM): filters on format compliance, temporal consistency and VLM-judged semantic grounding, cutting 1328K to 767K samples with 99.9%/99.6%/98.6% quality.

High-level planner (slow): NaVILA-style VILA (SigLIP + MLP projector + LLaMA3) takes history frames, the current frame and the goal image and generates the next sub-task text. SFT for 1 epoch, mixed with auxiliary data (EnvDrop summarization, ScanQA, ShareGPT-4V, Video-ChatGPT); frozen afterwards and called every 15 steps.

Low-level executor (fast): a semantic branch (CLIP RN50 text/vision encoders over plan, observation, goal) and a navigation branch (obs+goal channel-concatenated, ImageNet ResNet50) are fused by a 2-layer MLP. Fused features plus previous action go to a 2-layer GRU (128-d) and an actor-critic, trained with DD-PPO.
ZER reward: dense distance and view-angle shaping, sparse success reward, slack 0.01, success radius 1 m and 25°.

Wandering Suppression Penalty: adds -(path-length increment) and a voxel revisit penalty (voxel 0.25, weight 0.02), scaled by λ_w=0.2. It is enabled only after a ZER-reward warm-up, for about 10M more steps, to avoid stalling early exploration.

setting.backbone: NaVILA-style VILA (SigLIP + LLaMA3) slow planner, SFT-finetuned and then frozen; CLIP-RN50 + ResNet50 + GRU actor-critic executor trained with DD-PPO
setting.training_data: Planner: 767K self-built samples (RxR, xsR2R, YouTube) plus EnvDrop, ScanQA, ShareGPT-4V, Video-ChatGPT. Executor: Gibson 9000 episodes / 72 scenes, 20M steps of RL.
setting.observation: single egocentric RGB 128x128, 90° FOV, plus goal image; no depth/GPS/pose
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: MOVE_FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN_LEFT/RIGHT 30°, STOP
setting.simulator: Habitat (Gibson train; MP3D and HM3D cross-domain test); real Unitree Go2
setting.privileged: none at test time (geodesic distance is used only in the training reward)

numbers.eval_set_note: Gibson 4200 test episodes from 14 unseen scenes; 3 seeds averaged
numbers.extra: WSP reward, planner every 15 steps, 500 max steps, 1 m success radius

numbers.eval_set_note: 1000 episodes per difficulty level; trained on Gibson only, zero-shot transfer

numbers_note: Real-world results are qualitative only. The benchmark names Gibson-ImageNav, MP3D-ImageNav and HM3D-ImageNav are not on the canonical list; Gibson-ImageNav is the closest canonical name, and the MP3D/HM3D rows are labelled by the paper's own dataset names. The main-text MP3D SR (81.4) differs from the appendix table (81.1).
results: HRNav reaches 94.0% SR and 71.2% SPL on Gibson, beating REGNav (92.9/67.1), with larger gains on Hard episodes (SPL 66.8 vs 59.4). It generalizes zero-shot to MP3D (81.4/56.3 vs REGNav 78.0/50.2) and HM3D (80.0/49.3 vs 75.2/44.0). It also runs at 24 FPS and was demonstrated on a Unitree Go2.
limitations: Sim-to-real gap: camera settings differ from simulation, and quadruped embodiment (e.g., hind legs scraping furniture) is not modelled.
The planner call is slow (about 374 ms), so planning is sparse (every 15 steps), and a shorter interval trades latency for accuracy.
Real-world evidence is only a qualitative demo, and the dataset relies on noisy automatically generated annotations (only 58% retained after filtering).
